title: Make Time for What You Believe In
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When someone says they don't have time, what are they really saying?

groups.heading: How does he have so much time to do all this?

lines.text: I asked: how does he have so much time to do all this stuff? A student said: he has systems, and people who know their jobs. He probably hired people to help him put those systems in place, and really smart leaders.
I said you can try to put people in place and they don't execute. A student said: we also hold them accountable. I asked: but what does he do, as a person, to make them accountable?
A student said maybe it is the way he makes them feel, what he inspires. What is his leadership style, I asked? Another said: hard working, and people see that, so they want to follow.

I pointed to a talk the author had with a young man on a plane. As he retells it: you can't make fourteen thousand a year, we need to fix that, we're going to have different goals for you. He is sensitive. He sets goals. He is a motivator. He is charismatic.

groups.heading: He makes time for what he believes in

lines.text: If you go to somebody with a business idea and they say, I'm too busy, I don't have the time, I said: if you were sitting with the author and you had a genius idea, would he say, I don't have the time?
A student said: from what I've seen, he seems to make time for what he believes in, or for the things he thinks are important. What a great statement, I said. To make time.

I drew a picture. Imagine a bar graph with ninety percent of your time up at the top, making the company survive, driving sales. Then the money comes in and the company stabilizes, and it goes to eighty percent, then seventy, then fifty, because the company is self-sustaining. You know how to audit it. You have good people running it.

Then there is another bar, I said, that goes to twenty, thirty, forty percent, because you have the time and you have shifted your priorities to another initiative. Imagine the bar graph of the author's time, twenty bars across the page, shifting.
Where is your time going, and what do you make time for?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write how you spend your time now, in percent, across your projects.
Write what you make time for because you believe in it.
Write which project could run on its own with better systems and people.
Write the one person you must hold accountable, and how.
Write where you will shift your time next.

check.q: What did a student say about the author and time?
choices: He makes time for what he believes in
He hires others to do all of it

check.q: What did I say you can try and still not get?
What did I draw to explain time shifting?

recap: Make time for what you believe in. As a business runs itself, move your time to the next one.
